found.title: When a P re-representation and R's own re-representation have the same table, R's base-language program is dropped, so the solve and its 'used' field are credited to a learned symbol
found.explanation: In the R block, P's candidates are placed first, and R's own preimages are deduplicated against them by (kind, table) signature: `seen = {(kind, tuple(sorted(table.items()))) for kind, _, table, _ in first}; candidates = first + [c for c in candidates if (c[0], tuple(sorted(c[2].items()))) not in seen]` (lines 597-599). When the two collide, the element sub-search is the same, because the table is the same. The only things that change are which A gets lifted (`apply(Prim(kind), term, expr.term)`) and the attribution (`both = ... | set(learned_in(expr))`). So a task that the base-language scan solves in the same run gets P's symbol-built A instead. That A is larger, can differ from R's A on inputs outside the examples, and puts learned symbols into 'used'. Instrumentation shows that R's own candidates were dropped as duplicates in most FRESH-3 tasks where P supplied candidates (p_first=2, r_own=0 in 22 of 98 tasks that reached the R loop).

verdicts.title: When a P re-representation and R's own one have the same table, R's base-language program is dropped, so the solve and its 'used' field go to a learned symbol
verdicts.evidence: I read hybrid.py lines 595-599. When `first` (P's preimages) is non-empty, `seen` is built from P's (kind, table) signatures, and every R candidate with a matching signature is filtered out of `candidates`. The element sub-search depends only on the table, so the only things that change are the lifted A (`apply(Prim(kind), term, expr.term)`) and `used` (`how['used'] | learned_in(expr)`). To reproduce, I copied hybrid.py into work/verify-harness-p, added logging of the dropped and P-first candidates, and wrote my own driver (work/verify-harness-p/rep.py). It calls solve in-process at budget 3000 on fresh3::((append-k (dyn . 0) (static . 3)) (identify-geq-k (dyn . 1) (static . -7))), using the 19 Addendum 8 symbols from results/confirm.json. Results: gen0 SCfR -> re+map+search, used [], program (map (λ.1)) ((cons -1) x0), to_solution 314. Symbols in P only, SCfRP -> used ['s23_1'], program map(λ.1) over (fold-cons-nil ((cons -1) (fold-cons-nil x0))), to_solution 474. Both of R's own candidates, ((cons -1) $0) and ((cons 0) $0), were logged as dropped duplicates of P's s23_1-wrapped versions. The same swap happens with the 19 symbols in every space (SCfR used [] -> SCfRP used ['s23_1'], 322 -> 482).
verdicts.consequence: Two things change, and the verified/right counts do not. (a) Provenance: 'used' and any table that splits solves by whether a learned symbol (or a library-only symbol) was used will count some base-language solves as symbol-dependent. That inflates how much of P's or the library's lead is attributed to symbols. (b) The kept program is a larger, different A. In this example it is the same function (x++[-1] instead of [-1]++x under map(λ.1)), but in general it can differ off the examples, so it can move a task between sound, pool and right. to_solution also rises (314 -> 474), because P's spend comes before it. The primary sign test is on solves, and R2 is scored by ablation, not by 'used', so the distortion is bounded: low.
verdicts.fix: On a signature collision, keep R's own candidate. For example: `seen = {(c[0], tuple(sorted(c[2].items()))) for c in candidates}; candidates = [c for c in first if (c[0], tuple(sorted(c[2].items()))) not in seen] + candidates`. Or keep the current order but, when the signatures match, put R's expr in P's slot, so that the lifted A and 'used' come from the base or core program.

found.title: The library-tier gate is a cache of the teacher's answers: most accepted symbols are the verbatim verified program of one learning task, and the 'gain' is that same task found again by P
found.explanation: The gate is unchanged: accept when the family score rises, or stays equal while gate dreams rise. In the library tier the only extra cost is P's 1/20 share of the budget. compress.propose needs at least 2 tasks of use (min_tasks=2), and the dream compositions built from a target's own program meet that by themselves. So any closed whole-task program list[int]->X that the teacher found and the student missed becomes a 'symbol'. P then finds it at size 1 on exactly that task, and the score rises by that one task. That rise is true by construction, so the gate cannot reject such a symbol and tells you nothing about reuse. deepen.py had the same circularity, but there a whole-program symbol widened every search and the gate often turned it down. The two tiers take that brake away.

verdicts.title: Library-tier gate accepts verbatim whole-task programs of single learning tasks, found again by P (caching, not reuse)
verdicts.evidence: I recomputed this from work/tiny_two_tier_loop.json by diffing the solved sets of consecutive accepted student runs. All 11 acceptances into the library alone (s1_1-s5_1, s11_1, s12_1, s13_1, s17_1, s19_1, s25_1) follow one pattern. Every new solve has route 'symbols', the found program is the symbol's own definition (e.g. far/last -> '(lambda x0: list[int]. ((index (length (tail x0))) x0))' = s12_1), and each new solve is in proposed.support. real_tasks is 1 for 10 of them; s19_1 has 3 support tasks and gains 2 of them. Cycle 5's only acceptance is s25_1 (train/index-head, route symbols), so the loop went on to cycle 6 only because of it. The core acceptances (s6_1, s7_1, s9_1, s16_1, s21_1) and the s1_1 promotion behave differently: route 'search', the symbol used as a part, and solves outside the support. The code bears this out. hybrid.py lines 561-576 run P over admitted symbols plus integer constants only, so a closed list[int]->X symbol is a size-1 program on the exact task it was distilled from. The deepen3.py line 206 gate (score > score, or equal with more dreams) then rises by construction.
verdicts.consequence: In the library tier the gate cannot reject a cached whole-task program of a teacher solve, so it says nothing about reuse. Cached steps inflate the counts of accepted symbols, of cycles and generations, the per-generation steps scored for R1, and the loop's whole budget used as the R3 control (the last one makes the control more generous, not less). On FRESH-5 the pairing-only stratum can be solved by P as a composition of two cached symbols, so part of a pooled R3 lead could be teacher work carried over rather than vocabulary improvement. This is a bounded distortion of how the result reads, not a wrong verdict; fresh evaluation tasks are not themselves solved by the lookup.
verdicts.fix: Pre-register a class 'cached whole-task symbol': closed, single list[int] parameter, its new solves are a subset of its real support, and they come via route 'symbols' with program == definition. Report symbol counts, R1 steps and the primary comparison with and without these symbols, and stratify the evaluation by 'solution is a composition of cached symbols'. Alternatively, score the library-tier gate on learning tasks outside the symbol's real support (every minus support) plus the dreams.

verdicts.title: Learned constants have no tier: a library-only constant enters the elem and list spaces, so its library and core trials are identical
verdicts.evidence: deepen3.py lines 64-71: serialise (loop.py lines 95-104) moves a nullary symbol into `constants` and leaves it out of `abstractions`. spec_tiers then builds integers = base + learned constants and plain = base.primitives + int:c for all of them, and puts plain into keep['elem'] and keep['list'] whatever the core set is. names and listed never contain the constant, so the spec does not depend on whether it is in the core. tiny_two_tier_loop.json bears this out. student2.4l and student2.4c (s10_1 = (mul 2 5)) both have score 16.548 and spent 52069, and student4.6l and 4.6c (s24_1) both have 18.087 and spent 49885: the runs are identical. The 'library' trial still changed the list search (16.844 -> 16.548), which contradicts the docstring ('A library symbol is in no other search'; 'The element space never has a learned symbol'). If a constant were accepted in its library trial it would be recorded as core:false, and its promotion (strict rise on an identical spec) could never succeed. The related claim also holds: P's vocabulary (hybrid.py lines 454-456) has only admitted symbols and integer constants, so a symbol with no list[int] parameter cannot be fed the input in the library tier.
verdicts.consequence: Tier labels would misstate where an accepted constant acts: it widens the student's element and list searches while being reported as 'library alone, costs nothing'. This distorts the per-tier analysis and the R2 removal reading. Duplicate core trials waste student runs and enlarge the training ceiling and the whole-budget control. No constant was accepted in the tiny run, so nothing is wrong yet, but at real budgets it can happen.
verdicts.fix: Treat nullary symbols (and symbols with no list[int] parameter) as core-only: skip their library trial and record them as core. Alternatively, in spec_tiers (and deepen3_eval.spec_from_report) put only base integer constants in plain and add int:c to keep['list']/['elem'] only for constants in the core. Fix the docstring to match.

verdicts.title: FRESH-5 halves share 36 stage instances across roles
verdicts.evidence: fresh5.new_instances (lines 81-95) seeds and deals each (role, routine) on its own: Random(f'{SPLIT_SEED}:{role}:{routine}'), then [0::2] / [1::2]. I dumped both halves (dump.py -> development.json, registered.json; no solver run). v4.py: 653 registered tasks have novelty >0. 234 of them contain a registered-new instance that is also a stage of some development task, and 238 contain one that is a development-new instance in either role. 29 distinct registered-new instances actually used in tasks appear as development task stages (the reviewer reported 32 of 99; my distinct count is 83, so the details differ a little but the effect is the same). For list->list routines the two roles compute the same function. Exposure comes only through human development choices on fresh5dev (p_share, keep, tuning), not through the loop, which learns on the 214 learning tasks. So the primary R3 comparison is not contaminated, but the reading 'new parameter values never met in development' is false for about 36% of the new-instance tasks.

What did not break: P's vocabulary really is learned symbols plus constants only, with no base primitives (keep['symbols'] is filtered to admitted names); P is skipped when the library is empty; the registered set's task-level duplicate test against development and FRESH-4 tasks; strict.py's element-type comparison ([True] is not [1]); the share of programs that are wrong on the wide draw is similar across arms (about 15-19%), so the wide draw itself does not favour one arm; under section 12 neither P nor the two-tier vocabulary is a learned controller, value model or policy, and the dream tie-break counts whole solves of dreams, not partial credit, so neither is forbidden as such (only the missing hill-climbing control conflicts with section 12). Not done: no deepen3 run at real budgets, and no solver run on any FRESH-5 task, of either half.

found.title: The library gate is passed by memorising one teacher-solved task per symbol, so the library fills up and the loop does not stop
found.explanation: In the library tier a symbol is used only by P, and P costs the other searches nothing (budget//20, skipped when it finds nothing). So a closed whole-program symbol `lambda xs. <teacher's program for task T>` always raises the family-normalised verified score: P finds T by calling the symbol at about one candidate, and no other task is lost. Compression proposes exactly these symbols, because the dreams are built around the teacher's solutions and repeat them. The gate reads verified, not sound, so a teacher program that overfits a learning task becomes a symbol. No rule needs a library symbol to help any task outside the ones it was compressed from, and nothing caps the library except MAX_TRIALS=24 per cycle and MAX_CYCLES=12.
found.repro: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=<tree>:<tree>/exploratory/shift_loop_20261110 python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rsi-metaforge-core/49317f35-39aa-5636-a36c-c80f42cd346e/scratchpad/review15/work/find-design/tiny_gain.py <work>/tiny_two_tier_loop.json ; python3 <work>/find-design/closed_wrong.py (both read the author's toy deepen3 run; nothing is re-run)
found.observed: Toy run: 6 cycles, 5 of them accepting, 16 library symbols, 6 in the core. 11 of the 16 are closed list->X programs (s1_1..s5_1, s11_1, s12_1, s13_1, s17_1, s19_1, s25_1). Every library-alone acceptance gained exactly 1 or 2 learning tasks, each through route 'symbols' with the symbol alone, e.g. student1.4l gained 'validation/bool-identify-is-mod-k with k=2' through s4_1 = map(x -> is_prime(x+3) ? true : is_prime(x+5)). That symbol is wrong on x = 22, 30, -1, -3, ... s1_1 'odds' = filter(x==5 or is_prime(x+4)) is wrong on 11, 17, 21, ...; s13_1 'identify-is-mod-k k=2' is wrong on 5, 11, 17, .... Not one symbol is recursive (all depth 1). The loop stopped only in cycle 6. The training ceiling was 7.3M at the toy budgets.
found.consequence: At registered budgets the loop can keep accepting one memorised symbol per new teacher discovery until MAX_CYCLES. Then: (a) R1 'rises' on learning tasks and the R1 steps are made of lookup entries; (b) the loop's whole budget per task, one of the control's rungs, is not known in advance and may exceed what can be run; (c) on the 147 pairing-only registered tasks, whose stages are learning-task instances, P composes two memorised stage programs, so any lead there is memorisation by construction; (d) many of the admitted symbols are wrong programs that 'right' will reject, so the loop's signal and the registered measure point in different directions.
found.fix: Before registering, add one rule to the library gate: the gain must include at least one learning task outside the symbol's support (the tasks whose programs it was compressed from), or closed no-parameter symbols with one real support task are not proposed. Register a cap on the library size, and report for every accepted symbol whether its witness is sound on its own support tasks.

found.title: New parameter values do not remove the memorised-routine stratum: a third of FRESH-5 tasks still have a stage that is a symbol application
found.explanation: The plan relies on new parameter values to get past Addendum 8's finding that the lead sits where a stage equals a learned symbol. But learned symbols take integer parameters (append-k, remove-mod-k, take-k), so they cover every new k. The plan fixes the stagesym stratum only as a stratum beside a primary on all list tasks. So a 'confirmed' class, and any breadth ending, can again be carried by symbol-stage tasks.
found.observed: 'fresh5dev: 95 of 290 list tasks have a stage that is a symbol application'. Examples: append-k [-3], [-2], [2], [3], [4], [5], [7], [8], [9], [10], [12] = s23_1 [k]; remove-mod-k [-5]...[7] = s15_1 [|k|]; keep-mod-k [-1], rotate-k [0], replace-all-k-with-n [7, 7] = s18_1 [-2] (identity); reverse = s3_1. That is 33%, the same share as FRESH-4 (250 of 756 list tasks).
found.consequence: The 'one/two new instance' strata cannot be read as transfer beyond memorised routines. A confirmed primary on all list tasks would repeat Addendum 8: a lead carried by stages that are symbols, with a breadth reading that the data do not support.
found.fix: Register this rule: the final library's stagesym stratum is computed mechanically after the loop and before any evaluation run, and any claim beyond memorised routines is read only on list tasks with no symbol-application stage (a co-primary, or a gate on the class). Extend stagesym to stages that equal a composition of two symbols, and to whole pipelines that equal such a composition.

found.title: No arm separates the loop from P, from having many symbols, or from the directive's equal-budget hill-climbing control
found.explanation: Generation 0 has no symbol, so P never runs for it. 'The same machinery without learned symbols' therefore cannot tell what the loop chose from what P, or any set of symbols, would give. Section 12 also says 'No mechanism merged without its equal-budget hill-climbing control' (paragraph 7: best-so-far-conditioned random mutation at the identical candidate budget). The registered tally by function: 6 tasks marked '1 new instance' have 0 new by function, and 9 marked '2 new' have only 1. Development has the same pattern: remove-mod-k [-2] = seen [2], rotate-k [0], replace-all-k-with-n [7, 7].
found.consequence: Some tasks in the 'new instance' strata are really pairing-only tasks, or single learning-task functions, and these are exactly the tasks a memorised symbol solves. That inflates any 'new parameter' reading. 'Clean' holds only for instance identity, not for function or family.
found.fix: Define a new instance by its function on the pool plus the wide draw. Drop, or reclassify into the pairing-only stratum, any instance equal to a seen instance, the identity or a constant. State the claim scope as 'new parameter values of seen routines, on the FRESH input pool, with a mechanism chosen on FRESH-4 and possibly FRESH-5 dev'.

found.title: 'right' leaves the size of the wide domain and the step reading unspecified, and the gate optimises a different measure
found.explanation: _agrees skips every wide input on which the reference is undefined or exceeds VALUE_CAP, with no minimum, so for some tasks the wide test is nearly empty. Running out of 2,000 steps counts as a failure. On stored rows that rule bites only programs of the learned vocabulary, and Addendum 8's R3 turned on a single such task. Meanwhile the loop's gate reads verified, and strict.py gives exposed tasks only the audit, so nothing in the loop sees the measure the outcome is scored on.
found.repro: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=<tree>:<tree>/exploratory/shift_loop_20261110 python3 <work>/find-design/wide_domain.py f5dev ; python3 <work>/find-design/steps_rule.py (FRESH-4 stored rows, a development set)
found.observed: FRESH-5 dev, wide inputs in the domain out of 208: at least 150 for 242 tasks, 50 to 149 for 37, 10 to 49 for 19, 1 for 2 tasks (slice-k-n [3,3] then pow-k 9; slice-k-n [3,4] then pow-base-k 5). Sound programs that fail the wide draw only by steps: new@student 1, new@deploy 2, old 0, every generation-0 row 0. Wrong on the wide draw: new@student 23 of 126, gen0@top 18 of 117.
found.consequence: A margin of one or two tasks, typical of R3, can turn on an unregistered domain size or the step reading, applied to one arm only. The memorised overfit symbols of the first finding raise the gate's verified score and are rejected by 'right', so the loop's own rise and the outcome can diverge without anyone being able to say why.
found.fix: Register a minimum of in-domain wide inputs (e.g. 50; draw again with the same seed up to a fixed count, else mark the task 'thin' and report it apart). Report the step-out-not-a-failure reading in every row beside the primary. Report how many accepted symbols are unsound on their own support tasks, and R1 and R3 with those symbols removed.

found.title: R2 by removing each recursive symbol alone can again coincide with measured states and does not test 'built on'; a generation is not defined for library-only steps
found.explanation: If the last accepting cycle accepts exactly one recursive symbol r (as cycle 2 of Addendum 8 effectively did), 'final minus r' is the vocabulary of the previous cycle, which --cycles already evaluates. That repeats Addendum 8's coincidence. If the loop makes no recursive symbol (the toy run: 16 symbols, all depth 1, over 5 accepting cycles), R2 has nothing to score. Removing r tests whether r is used, not whether the gain depends on the earlier symbol. In the two-tier loop P would find a composition s_a(s_b x) of closed symbols anyway, so a recursive closed composition adds nothing. Promotions only consider symbols of the same cycle, so a cycle that only promotes cannot occur. But a cycle can change only P's library (toy cycle 5: one closed symbol, core unchanged) and still count as a generation for R1.
found.repro: python3 -c over <work>/tiny_two_tier_loop.json (printed in this review): every library entry depth 1; cycles [(1, 6 accepted, s1_1 promoted), (2, 4, none), (3, 3, none), (4, 2, none), (5, ['s25_1'], none), (6, [], none)]. Code: spec_from_report(upto=cycle) takes the cycle's core and the symbols with cycle <= upto.
found.observed: No recursive symbol in 5 accepting cycles. The cycle-5 generation differs from cycle 4 only by s25_1 = index(head xs) xs in P's library.
found.consequence: R2 can be 'met' by an ablation that is a state already measured, or 'failed' by absence, and neither reading tests dependence. R1 steps can be lookup entries for P.
found.fix: Score R2 as the final vocabulary against the final vocabulary with each recursive symbol's definition inlined (the earlier symbol removed when nothing else uses it), with 'final minus r' beside it. Register that an ablation equal to a measured state is reported as that state and counts once. Define a generation as the state after an accepting cycle, flag whether its core changed, and for more than two steps register the rule 'two consecutive steps each pass their sign test'.

verdicts.title: The library gate is passed by memorising one teacher-solved task per symbol, so the library fills up and the loop does not stop
verdicts.evidence: I read the author's toy deepen3 run (work/tiny_two_tier_loop.json) and deepen3.py. It ends with 16 library symbols, 6 of them in the core, all depth 1. Every acceptance into the library alone (student1.1l-1.5l, 2.5l, 2.6l, 3.1l, 3.5l, 4.1l, 5.1l) is a closed list->X symbol. Each gains about one learning task, solved through route 'symbols' by the symbol alone (for example s4_1 on 'validation/bool-identify-is-mod-k with k=2', s25_1 on 'train/index-head'). None of these was promoted. The gate (deepen3.py:206) compares family_score over verified programs, with no soundness check and no rule that the gain must reach a task outside the symbol's support. I checked the definitions by hand. s4_1 = map(is_prime(x+3) ? true : is_prime(x+5)) gives false for x=22 (25 and 27 are not prime), so it is wrong for 'is even'. s1_1 'odds' = filter(x==5 or is_prime(x+4)) drops 11 (15 is not prime). s13_1 = map(is_prime(x+4) ? 0 : 1) is wrong as 'identify-is-mod-k 2'. One small correction: P is not free when it misses. hybrid.py:579 adds its spent candidates to the total and so shrinks R's budget, but its cap is budget/20, so a single memorised task still wins. 'The loop does not stop' is not shown: the toy run stopped in cycle 6.
verdicts.consequence: At registered budgets the loop can turn each new teacher discovery into a lookup-entry symbol, some of them overfit. The 'rise' on learning tasks, and the R1 steps, would then be lookup growth. The loop's total budget, which is one rung of the control, cannot be known in advance. And the gate (verified) and the outcome measure (right) reward different symbols.
verdicts.fix: Add one rule to the gate for acceptance into the library alone: the gain must include at least one learning task outside the symbol's support tasks. Equivalently, do not propose closed symbols with no parameters whose real support is a single task. Register a cap on library size, and report for each accepted symbol whether its witness is sound on its own support tasks.

verdicts.title: New parameter values do not remove the memorised-routine stratum: a third of FRESH-5 tasks still have a stage that is a symbol application
verdicts.evidence: I re-ran stagesym.py with results/confirm.json on fresh5dev and got the same output: '95 of 290 list tasks have a stage that is a symbol application (98 of 300 tasks)', with append-k [k] = s23_1 [k] for 11 new k, remove-mod-k [-5..7] = s15_1 [|k|], rotate-k [0] and replace-all-k-with-n [7,7] = identity, and take-k = s2_1 [k]. Symbols that take integer parameters cover new parameter values by construction. The plan already has the stagesym stratum, but only beside a primary pooled over all list tasks.
verdicts.consequence: A lead on the 'one new' or 'two new' strata, or on the pooled primary, can again be carried by stages that are learned symbols. A reading of 'transfer to new parameters' would then repeat the over-reading of Addendum 8. This is a problem of interpretation: the stratum is already planned, so the data needed to read it correctly will exist.
verdicts.fix: Register this rule: the stagesym stratum is computed mechanically on the final library, after the loop and before any evaluation run. Any claim beyond memorised routines is read only on list tasks with no stage that is a symbol application, and that reading is a co-primary or a gate on the outcome class.

verdicts.title: The planned primary (R3 strict: final vocabulary at 10^4 against generation 0 at any budget) has almost no power under the development rates
verdicts.evidence: I re-ran find-design/power.py and got the reported numbers. With the Addendum 8 state's discordances the power is about 0.05. With the 19-symbol list scope it is 0.11 (n=175) to 0.31 (n=800). Only the 28-symbol union-listP variant, which was chosen on FRESH-4, reaches 0.97-0.99, and that falls to 0.24-0.60 if half or a quarter of the lead is lost on new-parameter tasks. The registered tally (regstrata_registered.out) gives 147 pairing-only tasks (139 with list outputs), not about 175. fresh5.make puts the whole FRESH-4 reserve first, so that number is fixed. Caveat: these rates come from other arms, measured with 'sound' rather than 'right', so they are indicative only.
verdicts.consequence: Under 'right' the most likely ending is 'not established' whatever the loop does, and the pairing-only stratum alone is near a coin flip even for the best variant. The result would still be readable as a null, but nobody would know in advance how weak a test it is.
verdicts.fix: Register the computed power and the smallest effect it can detect. Correct the pairing-only count to 147 (139 list). Fix outcome classes that cannot be over-read: lead beyond symbol stages / lead only on symbol-stage tasks / not separated / reversed.

verdicts.title: No arm separates the loop from P, from having many symbols, or from the directive's equal-budget hill-climbing control
verdicts.evidence: rsi5/OWNER_DIRECTIVE.md section 11 item 7 requires an equal-budget hill-climbing control of best-so-far random mutation for every mechanism arm. Section 12 says 'No mechanism merged without its equal-budget hill-climbing control'. The plan as stated has generation 0 (which has no symbol, so P never runs; hybrid.py:563 requires spaces['symbols'].admitted) and the Addendum 7 and 8 vocabularies with and without P. It has no ungated library of equal size and no mutation arm. In dev_after8_tiers.txt the same 28 symbols give 159 sound with P off and 169 with P on, so P alone moves about 10 tasks.
verdicts.consequence: A positive result cannot be credited to the loop's choices rather than to P plus the size of the vocabulary. Under the directive the result also could not support merging P or the two-tier loop.
verdicts.fix: Add cheap arms at 10^4: the final library with P off; the final library with every symbol in the core; an ungated library of the same size (the first N compress proposals on the loop's corpus) with P; and the hill-climbing arm (hybrid's E switch, or a mutation baseline) at an equal budget.

verdicts.title: Novelty strata are by name, not by function: some 'new' instances compute a seen function or the identity
verdicts.evidence: I wrote my own script (work/verify-design/inst.py, which reads only stage definitions) to compare each new instance with the seen instances, the identity and a constant on the FRESH pool plus a wide draw. Registered: identify-is-mod-k [-5] = seen [5] on pool and wide; identify-geq-k [-4] and [-2] = seen [-7] on the pool; first-stage keep-mod-k [-1] = identity; replace-all-k-with-n [-3,7] = identity on the pool; slice-k-n [6,-1] and [7,0], take-k [-1] and drop-k [-2] are constant. Development: remove-mod-k [-2] = [2], [-4] = [4], identify-is-mod-k [-3] = [3], rotate-k [0] and keep-mod-k [-1] = identity. new_instances (fresh5.py:76-95) filters by value at each position only, and the task-level duplicate test does not catch a stage that equals a seen instance. Per regstrata, 15 registered tasks (6 + 9) have fewer new instances by function than by name.
verdicts.consequence: About 15 of roughly 650 'new instance' tasks are really pairing-only or a step lower in novelty, and these are exactly the tasks a memorised or parametric symbol solves. That inflates the new-parameter strata by a bounded amount.
verdicts.fix: Define a new instance by its function on the pool plus the wide draw. Reclassify an instance that equals a seen instance into the lower-novelty stratum, and drop instances that equal the identity or a constant, or put them in a stratum of their own, before registration.

verdicts.title: 'right' leaves the size of the wide domain and the step reading unspecified, and the gate optimises a different measure
verdicts.evidence: The domain counts reproduce (fresh5dev: 242 tasks with at least 150 in-domain wide inputs, 37 with 50-149, 19 with 10-49, 2 with 1). But the wide draw is deterministic, seeded by the task name, so the code fixes its size once it is registered. A thin wide set only means that 'right' falls back to sound plus the whole pool, which is still a stricter measure, not a wrong one. Counting a step-out as a failure is written into strict.py's docstring and applies to every arm alike: a program that cannot return the output within the evaluator's budget is not right. That the loop reads only verifier verdicts on learning tasks, not 'right', is the study's own principle (no generating-function references in the loop), not a defect. The real part of this finding, overfit symbols passing the gate, is covered by the first finding.
verdicts.consequence: No number or comparison changes. At most, a reporting choice could be documented.
verdicts.fix: Optionally report the number of 'thin' tasks (fewer than 50 in-domain wide inputs), and a row with step-outs not counted as failures, beside the primary.

verdicts.title: R2 by removing each recursive symbol alone can again coincide with measured states and does not test 'built on'; a generation is not defined for library-only steps
verdicts.evidence: deepen3_eval.py has no R2 ablation at all. Its --cycles option evaluates spec_from_report(upto=cycle) after each accepting cycle, so a cycle that only adds a symbol to P's library counts as a generation. In the toy run, cycle 5 adds only s25_1 = index(head xs) xs, with the core unchanged. Every library symbol in the toy run has depth 1, so R2 as planned would have nothing to score there. The claim that 'final minus r' will coincide with an earlier cycle is speculative and was not reproduced: toy budgets do not show what real budgets will produce.
verdicts.consequence: R2 can end 'failed by absence', or as an ablation that equals a state already measured, and R1 steps can be library-only additions. That is a gap in the scoring rules rather than a distortion of a number.
verdicts.fix: Register three rules: what R2 scores when no symbol is recursive; that an ablation equal to a measured state is reported as that state; and that a generation is the state after an accepting cycle, with a flag for whether its core changed.
